To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the highest concentrations of Pb were observed at the highest Pb treatment in leaf, stem, and root.
the highest Pb concentration and the highest BCF were obtained at the highest dose of 50 mg Pb Kg -1 soil.

the highest Pb concentrations in Indian spinach leaf, stem and roots were obtained at 5 0 mg Pb kg - 1 soil treatment and that the highest values were 65.40 mg kg - 1 in leaf, 77.51 mg kg - ¹ in stem and 71.78 in mg kg -1 in root, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of Pb on growth of Indian spinach and the accumulation of Pb in different parts of the plants grown in soils of three textural classes.
the effects of different Pb levels on the growth and uptake of this vegetable crop in different types of soil.
the effects of different levels of lead on the accumulation and growth of Indian spinach in three different soils.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the growth of Indian spinach was inhibited by the application of Pb and the inhibition was dependent upon the soil texture.
the highest dose of applied Pb reduced the dry matter of Indian spinach, and increased the Pb accumulation in leaf, stem, root and bioaccumulation coefficient in all the three soils.
the highest dose of lead ( 50 mg kg -1 soil), the growth and accumulation of Pb in Indian spinach were significantly reduced in all the three textural groups of soil.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Indian spinach could be used as a potential plant for Pb removal from contaminated soil and it is a potential plant for the remediation of Pb-contaminated soil.
Pb application had negative effects on growth and accumulation of Pb in Indian spinach in three different textural groups of soil.
the highest concentration of Pb in leaf was found in sandy clay loam soil, followed by clay loam soil and the least in sandy loam soil.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bioconcentration factor of lead in Indian spinach was higher in clay loam than sandy loam and sandy clay loam soil.
Pb accumulation in Indian spinach grown in soils of different textures was significantly affected by soil texture.

the uptake and bioaccumulation of lead in Indian spinach were affected by soil textural group and the rate of Pb application, with the highest Pb concentrations and the lowest bioaccumulation factors obtained in sandy loam soil.
